title: Drive to Kyzart & horse-ride to Kilemche
desc: Your journey opens with a drive to Kyzart Village, in the hills below Song-Kol. A homemade lunch waits at a family homestay, and your guide walks you through the basics in the saddle before you set off.

The afternoon ride follows the Chaar-Archa River through wide, quiet valleys to Kilemche, an easy trail, a good chance to settle in with your horse. By evening you reach a herder family's yurt camp: wander the hills, breathe the air, and watch nomad life unfold before dinner.
meals: Lunch at guesthouse, dinner at yurt

title: Over Jalgyz-Karagai Pass to Song-Kol
desc: Today's ride asks a little more of you. After breakfast you climb toward the Jalgyz-Karagai Pass at 3300 m, a steady effort rewarded at the top by the first sight of Song-Kol shimmering far below.
You descend to the lakeshore past grazing herds and scattered yurts, reaching camp by midday. The afternoon is yours to walk by the water; after dinner, the night sky here is thick with stars.

title: Along Song-Kol to the western shore
desc: An easier day in the saddle, riding the open shore of Song-Kol. With two days behind you, your guide may pick up the pace to a canter across the smooth lakeside grass.

By midday you reach the Ozbek-Ashuu pasture on the western shore, where a nomad family serves lunch in their yurt, your home for the night. The afternoon is free to stroll the shore or take a short ride into the nearby hills.

title: Road trip to Tash-Rabat Caravanserai
desc: You leave the lake and drive south on a beautifully varied road, up over the Moldo-Ashuu Pass (3200 m), down to a streamside picnic, then through the small villages of the Ak-Talaa region.

Crossing the Mels Pass, the wide Arpa Valley opens out before you reach a cosy guesthouse near the 15th-century Tash-Rabat Caravanserai. After tea, walk up to this remarkable stone way-station and the hills around it.
meals: Breakfast at yurt, picnic lunch, dinner at guesthouse

title: Off-road to Kok-Kiya Valley
desc: Today you drive deep into the Kok-Kiya Valley, gateway to the hidden Kel-Suu Lake. The track threads through the villages of the At-Bashy region, framed by dramatic ranges, with a riverside picnic in the Bosogo Valley along the way.
You cross the high Kyndy Pass (3900 m) into the vast Ak-Say pastures, passing yurts and herds, and reach your guesthouse in Kok-Kiya by early evening, time for a gentle walk before dinner.
meals: Breakfast at guesthouse, picnic lunch, dinner at guesthouse

title: Trek to hidden Kel-Suu Lake
desc: One of the trip's great highlights. After breakfast you set off on a gentle trek, following a river through open valleys with mountains on every side and herds grazing in the distance.

About two hours in, Kel-Suu reveals itself, a startling lake hemmed by cliffs. Linger over a packed lunch and the views (an optional boat ride is possible) before retracing the trail to the guesthouse.
meals: Breakfast at guesthouse, picnic lunch, dinner at guesthouse

title: Road trip to Tash-Bashat Village
desc: You drive back out of Kok-Kiya toward Naryn through wide-open pasture country, reaching town around lunchtime for a warm meal and a short rest.

In the afternoon it's less than an hour on to Tash-Bashat, an authentic, untouristed village where you check into a comfortable hotel, a welcome change after yurts and mountain guesthouses. Stroll the streets, unwind, and enjoy a hearty dinner.
meals: Breakfast at guesthouse, lunch at restaurant, dinner at hotel

title: To Ysyk-Kol, cook lagman in Kochkor
desc: Today blends scenery and culture on the way to Ysyk-Kol. You climb over the Dolon Pass (3030 m), then stop in Kochkor to visit a local Dungan family and cook lagman, their famous hand-pulled noodle dish, and then eat the meal you helped make.
Driving on east to the lake, you reach a lakeside yurt camp with time for a swim. In the evening, head to the Ak-Say canyons to catch the sunset before returning for the night.
meals: Breakfast at hotel, lunch at guesthouse, dinner at yurt

title: South shore: eagle hunter, canyons & Jety-Oguz
desc: The day starts with an eagle-hunter demonstration, a window onto an old Kyrgyz tradition. From there you explore the dramatic, colour-streaked Fairy-Tale Canyons and stop in Tamga for lunch.
The afternoon takes in the Barskoon Waterfalls and the red sandstone of the Jety-Oguz Valley before you arrive in Karakol, time for a short wander through town before dinner.
meals: Breakfast & lunch at guesthouse, dinner at restaurant

title: Trek to Altyn-Arashan hot springs
desc: A short drive to Ak-Suu village, then you shoulder a daypack and set off up the valley to Altyn-Arashan. The trail follows a sparkling river through alpine forest, with a riverside picnic to break the climb.
By early evening you reach the gorge and your guesthouse. After a full day on foot, sink into the natural hot springs, then dinner and stargazing in the quiet of the mountains.
meals: Breakfast at hotel, picnic lunch, dinner at guesthouse

title: Hike to alpine Ala-Kol Lake
desc: The biggest day of the trip, and one of the most beautiful. On foot or on horseback, you head up from Altyn-Arashan, following the river before the trail turns into the forest and climbs toward Keldike Gorge.

A last, slippery push brings you to the Ala-Kol Pass (3900 m), where the turquoise lake and its glaciers spread out below. After photos and a rest, you descend back to Altyn-Arashan for the hot springs and dinner.
meals: Breakfast, picnic lunch & dinner at guesthouse

title: Trek out to Ak-Suu & drive to Bishkek
desc: A final morning on the trail, retracing the river and forest path down to Ak-Suu, one last lungful of mountain air. From there you drive to Karakol for lunch.

The road home runs along the northern shore of Ysyk-Kol, the "Pearl of Central Asia," reaching Bishkek in the evening, the close of a trip stitched together from horseback days, hidden lakes, and nomad hospitality.
meals: Breakfast at hotel, lunch at restaurant
